name: Mauve Blush
lede: Mauve Blush is a warm, dusty tan, filed under the mauve family though it reads as brown rather than purple, recorded by the Maerz and Paul dictionary in 1930 with a first use in 1928.

sections.title: A mauve that reads as tan
sections.body:
Our naming data files this as a family-word variant of [[mauve]] [1]. The Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930 plots it on plate 12 A3 and gives it a first recorded use of 1928, and the ISCC-NBS system files the same area as "light grayish yellowish brown" [1]. In LCH terms it reads as lightness 68, chroma 14, hue 71 degrees: a soft, low-saturation tan, closer to beige than to any purple [1].

Its nearest computed neighbors are [[mushroom|Mushroom]], [[linen-grey|Drab Grey]] and [[linen-grey|Linen Grey]], all within 3.5 units [2]. The closest everyday name is Tan, about 8.0 units away [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a close match covers enough of the canvas in 2,102, as photographed (1,422 by the stricter within-painting measure), which makes it more common than 93 percent of the named colors we track; it is one of the most widely present tones in our data [4]. [[painter:willem-van-de-velde-ii|Willem van de Velde (II)]] used it most: it appears in 4 of his 15 works here, 4.6 times the rate of the museums those works come from [4]. It is most over-represented in paintings from Nepal, at 2.9 times the expected rate (10 of 25 paintings), and on canvas it keeps company with [[taupe|Taupe]] and [[almond|Almond]] far more than chance [4].
